title: Fine-Cut Lemon Marmalade
summary: A pale golden, sharply tangy lemon marmalade with whisper-thin slices of peel, soaked overnight for a soft texture and natural set.
equipment: 7 × 250 ml glass jars with new lids
preserving pan or large heavy pan (at least 5 litres)
2 small plates, chilled in the freezer

steps.title: Slice
steps.text: Halve the lemons lengthways and slice them as thinly as you can, picking out every pip as you go. Tie the pips in the muslin; they release pectin while the marmalade cooks.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Put the sliced lemons, the muslin bag and the water in a large bowl, cover and refrigerate for 8-24 hours. Soaking starts to soften the peel and draws out more pectin.

steps.title: Cook the peel
steps.text: Tip everything into the pan and simmer gently, uncovered, for 40-50 minutes, until the peel is translucent and the liquid has reduced by about a quarter. Squeeze the bag into the pan and discard it.

steps.title: Sterilise
steps.text: Meanwhile, wash the jars and dry them in a 140 °C (120 °C fan) oven for 15 minutes.

steps.title: Set
steps.text: Stir in the sugar over a low heat until fully dissolved, then boil, stirring more often as it thickens, for 20-30 minutes until it reaches 104-105 °C and passes the cold-plate wrinkle test.

steps.title: Jar
steps.text: Skim off any froth, leave 10 minutes, then ladle into the warm jars with 5 mm headspace and close. Leave undisturbed overnight to set.

tips: Choose unwaxed lemons, or scrub waxed ones in hot water, as the peel stays in the marmalade.
Slicing the lemons as thinly as possible is the biggest factor in a delicate texture.
A common mistake is stirring hard during the final boil, which clouds the jelly; stir gently and only to stop sticking.
Meyer lemons give a sweeter, more floral version with the same method.
storage: Unopened jars keep in the fridge for up to 3 months, or in a cool cupboard for up to 1 year if processed in a boiling-water bath for 10 minutes. Once opened, refrigerate and use within 1 month. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
